Add to the agenda please BTW is there pm issue for this call? https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/pull/37 sorry stuck on another call what is the types_section in the code section? i think more examples in the spec would be good 🙂 type section is the section that defines the function types: num inputs/output and max_stack_height it seems duplicated though here, the code section has type_section but also inputs/outputs/max_stack_height i think max_stack_height is not really required to be in the header either, as it is inferred during validation Yes, but it is recursive. And runtime needs it. But I may have a "fix" for this 😉 why don't the types just go in the code section header? This comes from the fact that (at least initially) the section header was a generic concept: kind+size. You could have a generic parser for EOF which was able to split the container into kind+body of sections. This also explains the terminator a bit. Later we landed the optimization allows singular sections (e.g. data) and arrays of sections (e.g. code). The optimization remove repeating the kind byte multiple times. The current design is a bit of middle ground between being fully generic and fitting the encoding precisely to EOFv1 needs. hmm, i don't really get it 😅 -- doesn't having `num_code_sections` mean that you already don't need to repeat the `code` kind? Yes. This was different originally. in that case i think the format will be simpler to inline the type into the code section header (since you won't need to check that `len(types_section) == len(code_sections)`) but, correct me if i am missing something. i updated this to incorporate bounded VLQ values and the new sentinel value for non-returning functions (<@275684146658148352> <@403707149043105803> <@425274498732916736> ) Header or body? It is difficult to have it in the header because an entry is either `kind+size` or `kind+n+sizes`. Anyway, I try to focus on what is needed and by what. How to exactly encode this information can be decided later. the start of the code section (in the EOF body) Yes, <@403707149043105803> proposed this. **EOF Implementers Call 30** https://youtu.be/h7sDi6APa0Y it's good to have all the types parsed before starting to validate sections (they are required to validate CALLF/JUMPF), so it's convenient to have them compactly in one place i added a reference vlq implementation here https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/pull/37/commits/69ebc5013638974257d07a81dee7289b51dd270f the signed integer vlq encoding was surprisingly tricky to get right. i ended up using zigzag (which essentially stores the sign bit in the lsb). re. performance -- the reference vlq decode implementation is actually comparable in performance to the python builtin from_bytes https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/pull/37#issuecomment-1885735155. so, i don't think that is going to cause very much interpreter overhead.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
This comes from the fact that (at least initially) the section header was a generic concept: kind+size. You could have a generic parser for EOF which was able to split the container into kind+body of sections. This also explains the terminator a bit. Later we landed the optimization allows singular sections (e.g. data) and arrays of sections (e.g. code). The optimization remove repeating the kind byte multiple times.

The current design is a bit of middle ground between being fully generic and fitting the encoding precisely to EOFv1 needs.
